title: Successful human puzzle players voiced qualitative explanations more often than language agents
summary: In an ARC-AGI-3 trajectory study, qualitative descriptions appeared in 72 of 144 successful human runs and 17 of 119 successful runs from three agent systems. The human data came from think-aloud recordings and the model data from agent traces. The comparison measures recorded descriptions in successfully completed games.
ai_technology: GPT-5.6 Sol assisted analysis; ARC-AGI-3 agent traces
organization: Nanyang Technological University; Technical University of Darmstadt; Basis Research Institute; Harvard University; Cornell University

source_review.scope: v1 annotation workflow, participant selection, Section 4 trajectory results

evidence.tested: The authors collected 144 human trajectories across 64 participants and 25 games, collected 250 publicly released model trajectories, and analyzed successful subsets. They spot-checked parts of the model-assisted annotation.
evidence.unknown: Differences in what humans say aloud and what agents write or log limit claims about underlying cognitive representations.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-5.6 Sol implemented trigger detectors and annotated cognition from aligned transcripts and game traces. Learned agent trajectories supplied matched-task comparison material.
